newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold again despite crude slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold again despite crude slide.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices held relatively steady again Friday in thin trade, with bearish sentiment from another steep slide in crude partly offset by a fairly balanced market ahead of some warmer weather next week.
"If you look at supply and demand, we're pretty much in balance, and next week, we could get the first heat of summer," said one cash trader.
But with crude breaking down this week, most agreed buyers seemed more relaxed than sellers.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still talked at $16.00-25 a barrel though some thought buyers may have retreated to the high-$15s, traders said.
NYH July one percent paper was pegged only slightly lower at $16.00-20, pressured by crumbling crude, with August quoted about even with July, traders said. September paper was seen at $15.85-16.00.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour notionally held steady at $16.50-75. Traders said a 0.3 HP barge (delivered New England) sold at a formula cargo high plus $1.
High sulphurs in New York also held steady, with 2.2 percent still talked in the low-$15 area, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices notionally were stable, with one percent at $16.00-25 and three percent at $14.50-75.
Traders said a Florida utility awarded the 1.8 percent percent portion of its tender at $16.25 (delivered).

New York city gate gas prices edged up slightly Friday to about $2.40/mmBtu, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was little changed at about $2.18/mmBtu, or $13.73 a barrel.
